sheets.name: README
rows: Traceability view for one regulation-to-SHACL generation run.
Generation is frozen before RDF execution; no ship graph or hidden expected outcome is used here.
events.jsonl is append-only; CSV and Excel sheets are derived views.
Static validation passed and the semantic validator accepted the candidate.
No verified canonical term was available; the generator was not allowed to invent one.
Accepted shapes await the separate bulk evaluator.

sheets.name: RUNS
rows: The candidate faithfully encodes the requirement: it targets ships, preserves the false-exposure alternative, requires protection and continuous accessibility for exposed valves of the specified types, and provides a non-applicable exposed branch for other valve types. Canonical terms, datatypes, SHACL structure, ownership, and namespace are valid.

sheets.name: ITERATIONS
rows: The conditional alternatives are incomplete and create accidental fail logic: an exposed valve whose valveType is not isolating, pressure, or vacuum is outside the regulatory condition but cannot satisfy either branch. Add a non-applicable branch for valveExposed=true with valveType outside the controlled set (or otherwise encode the negated applicability condition), while retaining the existing false-exposure branch and requiring iceAccretionProtectionPresent=true and continuouslyAccessible=true only when valveExposed=true and valveType is in the specified set.

The prior repair is present but implemented with reversed logic: IMO_055_ExposedNonApplicableBranch currently raises a violation when valveType is outside {isolating, pressure, vacuum}, so it is satisfiable for an in-set type and allows an applicable exposed valve to bypass iceAccretionProtectionPresent=true and continuouslyAccessible=true. Change that branch to accept only valveExposed=true with valveType outside the controlled set (for example, make its SPARQL constraint select/violate in-set values, or use an explicit negated in-set shape), while retaining the false-exposure branch and the applicable branch. No vocabulary matcher is needed.

The candidate faithfully encodes the requirement: it targets ships, preserves the false-exposure alternative, requires protection and continuous accessibility for exposed valves of the specified types, and provides a non-applicable exposed branch for other valve types. Canonical terms, datatypes, SHACL structure, ownership, and namespace are valid.
